Cluster-vetted: representative entries in this cluster were read against the vendored Rails body; the rest share the same mechanism and were classified by it, not line-diffed individually.

Satisfied by a different path: Rails keys `@leases` by `ActiveSupport::IsolatedExecutionState.context`, which returns the current Thread/Fiber object (connection_pool.rb:711). JS has no thread objects, so trails keys the registry by the AsyncLocalStorage-backed numeric id from `executionContextId()` (connection-pool/execution-context.ts) — the direct analogue of `.context`, named for what it returns. Same lookup, no Ruby-thread equivalent to call.
